meta.title: Perspectives — Priya Vishwanathan
meta.description: What thirty-five years taught Priya Vishwanathan about guests, teams and standards, in her own words.

sections.label: Perspectives
sections.sub: What thirty-five years taught her about guests, teams and standards, in her own words, from two conversations recorded in 2026.

sections.label: Convictions
sections.title: In her <t>own words.</t>

items.q: “Every time a guest has complained and been not so polite to me, it was a learning: what we had to correct and what we did wrong.”
“If you’re not working with data… that’s more of a dictatorship.”

items.t: Luxury is what your guest says it is.
items.q: “What luxury means to your customer will come from data.”

items.t: Good to great touches the heart.
items.q: “I was in a business, not in a charity. Good to great really happens when you do something that touches somebody’s heart.”
“If you have to respect others, you’ve got to first respect yourself.”
“We don’t hire for skill, we hire for attitude.”
“Reinvention is the name of the game.”

sections.src: Transcribed from HospeTalk, episode 35, and Inspire Someone Today, episode 180.

sections.label: Three questions every leader should ask their team

items.k: What can you do to make the wrong become better?

sections.label: The Indian guest today, as she sees it

items.t: Today’s Indian traveller is often more travelled than the foreign guest, and expects the real thing: a Mexican dish had better be Mexican.
Ready to spend on a unique experience, not just on a name. Indian hotels now compete for the Indian guest.
A more demanding guest means young front-line teams need the confidence, and the backing, to draw a line.
